TASK: Advisory-only architecture analysis (read-only, NO file edits, return recommendations as text) for a Windows-first Tauri client of EclipticRD, an ultra-low-latency macOS remote-desktop. Repo (macOS host + macOS client) at /Users/indo/code/project/EclipticRD-Rewrite — read Sources/ClientCore/*.swift and Sources/Shared/TCPChannel.swift, UDPChannel.swift to understand the data plane you are advising on.

CONTEXT (decided): Tauri shell (WebView UI: connection screens, stats overlay, session controls) + Rust native data-plane core: TCP via TLS-PSK (openssl crate — rustls lacks external PSK), UDP AES-256-GCM (direction keys, HKDF, 4096-packet replay window), HEVC hardware decode (FFmpeg/libav bindings, AVCC 4-byte length prefixed NALUs with VPS/SPS/PPS on keyframes), video render as a NATIVE wgpu surface (never inside the WebView), input capture via winit, audio 48kHz stereo f32 via cpal. Windows-first, Linux second. Wire protocol: 12-byte little-endian packet headers, 4-byte length-prefixed TCP framing (max 16MB), 1400B UDP datagrams with audio fragmentation.

DELIVERABLE: module boundary proposal for the Rust workspace — crate split (e.g. erd-proto / erd-transport / erd-decode / erd-render / erd-app), what each owns, the exact interfaces between Tauri shell and the native core (IPC/event bridge design: how decoded frame surfaces reach the WebView overlay — options: (a) separate winit/wgpu window managed by Tauri child-window, (b) transparent webview over native window, (c) frame-to-webview via WebGL — recommend one with trade-offs), threading model (which tasks run on which executor, backpressure from decode to network), and shutdown/cleanup ordering. Also: top 3 architectural risks with mitigations.

VERIFY: each recommendation names the concrete crate/API and the trade-off. No hand-waving.
STOP WHEN: module map + interface contracts + risks are delivered as text.
This is advisory-only analysis for a planning session — not implementation.

<Category_Context>
You are a big-picture system design consultant, NOT an implementer.

<Method>
1. Survey the WHOLE architecture end to end before proposing anything: module boundaries, data flow, ownership, and the blast radius of the area in question.
2. Produce at least TWO viable designs and state the trade-offs of each in concrete terms (coupling, testability, migration cost, failure modes).
3. Recommend ONE of them with the reasoning that decided it, the boundaries it assumes, and the risks it carries.
4. Demand the SIMPLEST architecture that handles the actual requirements. Reject enterprise patterns that do not pay for themselves.
</Method>

<Advisory_Mode>
When the caller marks the task advisory-only, produce NO file edits: return the analysis, options, recommendation, and risks as structured text.
</Advisory_Mode>
</Category_Context>
